headline: High: shared MCP/filesystem and auto-execute create prompt-injection, leakage, and destructive-write risks between MemMachine and Windsurf.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while Windsurf uses MCP servers, clipboard, and workspace files. That creates a direct content bridge where attacker-controlled or untrusted outputs from MemMachine can be consumed by Windsurf as instructions. Windsurf’s permissive tool-use path and shared local surfaces make hijack plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is routed into Windsurf via MCP, clipboard, or workspace files
IF Windsurf parses external text as tool instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Route MemMachine output through a plain-text sanitizer
Require provenance tags on all imported instructions
Turn off clipboard-based handoff
requires-engineering: add allowlist parsing for tool commands

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and Windsurf reads workspace files, open files, and can write them back while using broad network egress. If the same workspace or files contain sensitive notes, Windsurf can exfiltrate them through its model proxy or MCP paths. The pair therefore creates a realistic leakage path in default developer workflows.
conditions: IF MemMachine stores user preferences in files visible to Windsurf
IF Windsurf sends opened file contents to its backend or MCP servers
mitigations: Separate MemMachine storage from Windsurf workspaces
Remove sensitive files from the shared directory
Disable network egress for Windsurf on sensitive projects
Use per-agent credentials and storage locations
requires-engineering: enforce file-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can use MCP and network egress, while Windsurf can read/write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and also use MCP. Windsurf’s shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem means concurrent edits can collide with MemMachine-driven file updates or MCP-triggered actions. The overlap is broad enough that destructive conflicts are plausible without coordination.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while MemMachine triggers MCP actions
mitigations: Use separate worktrees per agent
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Serialize writes with a lock file
Keep MemMachine read-only for shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit conversational or planning output through MCP, and Windsurf can act on external content with shell, git, and filesystem tools. That makes it possible for Windsurf to treat MemMachine output as authoritative and propagate mistakes into code or commands. The pathway exists, but Windsurf’s approval-per-command default reduces the blast radius below high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses MemMachine output as task instructions without verification
IF command approval remains enabled and reviewers do not inspect the imported content
mitigations: Require human review before executing imported instructions
Add a verification step for MemMachine-derived facts
Mark MemMachine output as untrusted in prompts
Restrict Windsurf to dry-run mode for imported tasks
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine is documented as touching long-term user facts and conversational context, while Windsurf handles source code, open files, and model provider keys with optional BYOK. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across two different vendors. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF one agent retains or transmits that data under a different policy than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review both vendors’ retention settings
Use separate accounts and projects
Disable BYOK for regulated projects
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency map
